svg.title: Ceiling water damage, from a stain to a collapse risk
svg.desc: Four severity levels. A dry, stable brown ring means find the source and monitor it. A damp stain that is still spreading means call now while the drywall can still be dried. Bubbling or peeling paint means water is pooling above the surface and the room should be cleared below it. A sagging, bulging or dripping ceiling means leave the room immediately, because saturated drywall can come down as one sheet.
svg.text: When a stain stops being a stain
Saturated drywall holds a surprising amount of water and lets go all at once.

g.text: An old leak that may already be fixed. Find the source before you paint over it.
Active leak. Call while the drywall can still be dried instead of replaced.
Water is pooling above the paint film. Move what is underneath out of the room.
Leave the room now and keep people out. Saturated drywall drops as one sheet.
